To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the additional energy cost of using SCA countermeaturs is between 10% and 30% and that using lightweight block cypers can reduce the energy cost by 20% and 40% when compared to AES.

the energy consumption of AES with first and second order masking is approximately 2x higher and the energy consumption of using lightweight block cypers with Boolean masking is approximately 1.5x higher than the energy consumption of the AES algorithm without any SCA countermeasurers.

the energy consumption of SCA countermeasured implementations is significantly higher (up to 1000%) than implementations without SCA countermeasurers, that the energy consumption is also significantly higher (up 1000%) when using lightweight block cipers than AES, that the energy consumed by AES is significantly higher than the energy consumed by the lightweight block ciphers (up to 2000%), and that the energy consumed when using the lightweight block cipers is significantly higher when using Boolean first order masking
In summary, our research is concerned with
providing a methodology for developing energy models of cryptographic software and using these models to assess the additional energy overhead of SCA countermeases on 32 bit ARM devices.
providing an accurate and efficient way of modelling the energy consumption of cryptographic algorithms with and without SCA counterme.

the following: 1) Developing an ISA based statistical energy model that can accurately predict the energy consumption of cryptographic software on embedded devices 2) Evaluating the energy consumption of SCA countermeures on embedded devices and 3) Evaluating the additional energy consumption that using lightweight block cipters on embedded devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the energy consumption of SCA countermeasured implementations of AES and implementations of lightweight block ciphers are comparable to that of non-countermeasured implementations of these algorithms.
the use of lightweight cryptography on 32-bit microcontrollers does not reduce energy consumption when compared to using AES with masking countermeasures.
using lightweight cryptography is not a viable solution to reduce energy consumption on 32 bit devices.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
using lightweight block ciplhers can save up to 50% in energy consumption and that using SCA countermeases can add up to 50%.
we provide an energy model of a cryptographic implementation that is accurate to +/- 5% and that we use it to compare the energy consumption of SCA countermeures, AES, PRESENT, KELIN and ZORO.
the energy model we developed is accurate enough to provide an energy comparison for different SCA countermeasure techniques and lightweight ciphers on embedded devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the additional energy consumption due to SCA countermeases is not significant compared to the energy consumption of lightweight ciphers.
using lightweight cryptography is a better option than implementing AES with SCA countermeatues on 32 bit ARM Cortex-M4 devices.

lightweight ciphers can reduce the energy consumed by an AES implementation on an embedded device by as much as +/- 50%, however, this reduction in energy consumption is dependent on the SCA countermeasure used.
